open_obligations: Note that a martingale allows individual wrong-to-right cases, so the conflict is about averages.
Check that Du et al.'s agents satisfy condition (1).
Check the empirically flat accuracy trajectories Choi et al. report on Du-like tasks.
in.other_title: Multi-agent debate as a martingale: expected belief in the correct answer is unchanged
in.rationale: Du et al. conclude from qualitative cases where all agents start wrong but end right that debate does not only amplify an initially present correct answer. Choi, Zhu and Li prove that under their Dirichlet-multinomial model with Bayesian count updates and condition (1), belief in the correct answer is a martingale, so debate alone does not raise expected correctness; individual cases can still go wrong-to-right under a martingale.
in.scope: proposed CHALLENGES: whether multi-agent debate itself improves correctness beyond amplifying initial answers
